questions.question: Does _put_to_queue drop exactly two oldest entries when full before inserting the overrun frame and triggering event?
questions.answer: Yes. The new implementation loops `for _ in range(2): q.get_nowait()` then calls `q.put_nowait(overrun)` then `q.put_nowait(item)` — with no try/except swallowing failures on the final inserts.

questions.question: Is the overrun frame placed immediately before the triggering event in the queue?
questions.answer: Yes. `q.put_nowait(overrun)` runs before `q.put_nowait(item)`, so draining the queue always yields [..., overrun, item] at the tail.

questions.question: Does test_overflow_preserves_newest_event assert that new_event is last and overrun is second-to-last?
questions.answer: Yes. `assert items[-1] is new_event` and `assert items[-2].get('event') == 'overrun'` — both checked against the drained list.

questions.question: Do all 74 pre-existing tests still pass after this change?
questions.answer: Yes. Full suite runs 75 tests (74 from story 01 + 1 new) — all pass. test_broadcast_overrun_drops_oldest_and_inserts_overrun_frame still passes because it only requires at least one overrun frame, which the new code still produces.

questions.question: What happens if the queue has only 1 item when overflow is triggered?
questions.answer: The `for _ in range(2)` loop catches QueueEmpty on the second iteration and breaks. Then overrun and item are both enqueued — queue ends up with 2 items. No exception is raised.

questions.question: Is there any remaining path in _put_to_queue where the triggering event could be silently discarded?
questions.answer: No. The final `q.put_nowait(item)` has no try/except. If after dropping 2 items the queue is somehow still full (only possible if maxsize <= 2), it will raise QueueFull rather than silently drop — a fail-loud behavior. For normal maxsize=256 this cannot happen.
